subject: MAP draft & alignment on close window + procurement signature runway
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: MAP draft & next steps (post-demo)

Hi Laura — great to meet you and Evan on the demo this morning. Quick recap and a suggested MAP attached (shipwright-mutual-action-plan-v3.xlsx). High-level items we agreed:

- Target outcome: integrate Redwood inference for real-time fulfillment scoring in two US regions (East/West) by end of April.
- Pilot scope: 3 models (rerank + gen-lite + embeddings), integration via API + dedicated capacity for the pilot.
- Acceptance criteria: 95th pct latency < 300ms, baseline token cost target under $0.002/token for the pilot workload.

Attached MAP draft includes milestones, owners, and a proposed signature runway. Two asks for you: (1) confirm procurement/contract sign-off target (we noted April 30 during the call but you mentioned procurement churn), (2) flag any internal dependencies we missed on your side.

Short proposed milestone rundown (from MAP v3):
- Week of Apr 9: Technical kickoff + test dataset handoff (Owner: Shipwright - Evan)
- Week of Apr 16: Integration + validation on staging (Owner: Mateo / Shipwright eng)
- Week of Apr 23: Performance tuning, cost forecast, final SOW adjustments (Owner: Redwood PM - Neha)
- Week of Apr 30: Contract signature + deployment to pilot prod region (Owner: Shipwright procurement; Redwood legal)

If April 30 is aggressive for procurement, we can shift to May 15 as a fallback — please advise.

Thanks — I’ll be available all week for follow-ups.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
+1 415-555-0118

Thanks Mateo — good recap and appreciate the clear milestone layout. Evan and I reviewed the MAP and procurement reality at Shipwright is: our legal/finance review window is 2 full weeks once a final SOW is submitted to Procurement, then the PO cycle is another ~5 business days. We have an internal board meeting week of May 6 where we need to show vendor costs locked to the pilot to get budget sign-off.

Concrete asks from our side:
- Can Redwood commit to a finalized SOW by Apr 20 so we can route it through Procurement in time for the May 6 board package?
- On the MAP, please add a discrete "Procurement packet prepared" milestone with owner Redwood (Neha) and date Apr 20.
- We also need a short technical appendix describing data retention, audit logging, and key management (HSM/KMS). Evan, can you confirm any additional compliance items?

One constraint: our legal has indicated that signature by Apr 30 is unlikely unless the SOW is finalized by Apr 18 and Procurement prioritizes the packet. Best-case signature window is May 8–12. Worst-case is late May if any redlines appear.

We want to keep April as the kickoff month for internal work, but the official contract sign-off will likely fall into the early May window.

Happy to hop on a 20-min call tomorrow if it helps.

—Laura
VP Product Operations | Shipwright
laura.chen@shipwright.ai

2) "Legal quick-response lane" — propose a 48-hour SLA from Redwood legal for minor redlines (non-substantive) to help compress your procurement timeline. We can add this as an optional term in the MAP so Procurement sees the commitment.

Proposed adjusted milestones (dates):
- Apr 13: Kickoff + dataset handoff (Shipwright)
- Apr 20: SOW final + Procurement packet prepared (Redwood lead: Neha Kapoor)
- Apr 23–26: Staging validation + perf tuning (Redwood eng + Shipwright)
- May 8–12: Target signature window (Procurement + Legal)

If Shipwright can prioritize final SOW review by Apr 18, we expect signature in the May 8–12 window. If Shipwright needs an April signature for internal constraints, we can push extra legal hours but would need to confirm scope freeze by Apr 14.

I attached a one-pager compliance appendix we typically include with Procurement packets — I'll drop that into the shared folder after this thread.
